|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | main talk | Title | Title. Say: this is the Oct 25 update. Main results are on Amazon Reviews 2023 Electronics only. The headline system is now a frozen LLaMA probe plus an Evidence model, combined by a Reflector. |
| 2 | main talk | The Problem: Why Single-Pass LLMs Fail | Problem. Single-pass LLM rating has no evidence check. Keep it short: 1 minute. |
| 3 | main talk | From Passive Classifier to Agentic System | Research question and gap. Wang et al. 2025 is the baseline paper. Our question: does adding a second, independent signal and a combiner beat a single model? |
| 4 | main talk | Key Terms: Models and Agents | Key terms 1. Do not read the table. Say: these are the names you will hear; the three to remember are the LLaMA probe, the Evidence model and the Reflector, which together make the main stack. Come back to this slide when a question uses a term. |
| 5 | main talk | Key Terms: Data, Evaluation and Method | Key terms 2. Point at four: balanced eval vs natural test (why two numbers), gate (rule written before running), label leak (why old numbers were withdrawn), and the deletion test (how explanations are checked). |
| 6 | main talk | The Project at a Glance | AT A GLANCE. Read the three cards left to right. Must say the caveat: against the old stack refit on the same 2,000 dev rows the gain is only 2.0 / 1.5 points and not significant. |
| 7 | main talk | Amazon Reviews 2023 Electronics: Frozen, Disjoint Splits | Protocol. Frozen disjoint splits; all choices on dev; each test split read once per declared config. Since Oct 24 there is also dev2 (2,000 balanced) for the Reflector. |
| 8 | main talk | How One Experiment Flows, From Rule to Paper | Workflow. Six steps for every experiment: declare in LOG.md, run resumably, gate on dev only, read the tests once, freeze, record and back up. Say: 16 failures are reported and none touched the test sets, which is why the one pass can be trusted. |
| 9 | main talk | Phase 1: LLaMA-3-8B + LoRA Fine-Tuning | LoRA explained. LoRA is still trained (Phase 1), but in the final stack it is an ablation row, not the main agent. |
| 10 | main talk | The One-Shot Label Leak Inflated Earlier Numbers | Leak audit. Picking a one-shot example whose star differs from the truth leaks about 8 points. All later numbers are zero-shot and leak-free. |
| 11 | main talk | Where Phase 2 Started: the Original Four-Agent Design | Original Phase 2 design (Analyst, Visual, RAG, Critic). Say: this was the starting design; the audit (appendix slide 38) and later experiments replaced it with the probe + Evidence + Reflector system (slide 16). Slide 20 shows how the agent idea comes back in Phase 2 v3. |
| 12 | main talk | What the Electronics Adapter Actually Generates | Hallucination study. LoRA explanations are a canned template; digit probabilities are the usable signal. That is why Phase 2 combines probabilities, not explanations. |
| 13 | main talk | Everything We Tried and Dropped (1 / 2) | Full ledger, part 1. Do not read every row. Pick three: the LLM judge (failed twice, which is why the LLM does not decide the star), the Visual Verifier (constant output), and the recalibration (the gain was the leak). Say: every rule was written before the run, on dev data only. |
| 14 | main talk | Everything We Tried and Dropped (2 / 2) | Full ledger, part 2. Message: more views of the same text, more LoRA data and fancier Reflectors did not help; what helped was more data for the probe and a bigger Reflector fit set. Note the honest near-miss: the 10K probe missed by .001 and only the 40K version passed. |
| 15 | main talk | What We Kept, and the Evidence for It | What we kept. Walk the ten rows quickly: each change has its evidence on the right. Together they give the main stack, 67.5% balanced eval and 75.7% natural test. |
| 16 | main talk | Main System: LLaMA Probe + Evidence Model Stack | MAIN RESULT. Probe + Evidence stack 67.5 eval / 75.7 natural, macro-F1 .675 / .612. Variance 65.8 +/- 0.6 and 75.4 +/- 0.8. Read the honest-read band aloud. |
| 17 | main talk | How Far Phase 2 Moves the Baseline | Phase 1 to Phase 2. Lead with the gain: +13.5 points on balanced eval and +22.3 on natural test, i.e. 29% and 48% fewer errors. Then be fair to Phase 1: it gets the direction right (within one star 94%, positive vs negative 91-93%); the exact star is the hard part. Its 53.4% on natural test is a class-mix effect: trained balanced, while 65% of natural reviews are 5-star. On its home data with the paper's protocol, leak-free, it reaches 69.1% (always-5 already gives 63.8%). Do not quote the old 70.7 / 60.1: they used the leaky prompt. |
| 18 | main talk | All Models, Exact Accuracy with 95% Bootstrap CI | Bar chart of all frozen models with 95% CIs; main stack in red. Point out: base LLaMA zero-shot is weak (34%) but a probe on its hidden states reaches 61 / 74. |
| 19 | main talk | Does the Result Hold Up? Corrections, Errors, Calibration, Cost | Robustness. After Holm correction 5 of 8 comparisons stay significant, including the main stack vs the earlier LoRA + Evidence stack on both splits. Most errors are one star off. Calibration is good (ECE .05-.06). The probe costs 0.67 s per review, the rest is under 0.1 ms: that is why the next step adds a Router. |
| 20 | main talk | Agents That Route, Explain and Check Themselves | Next: Phase 2 v3. Say: the specialists decide the star because an LLM choosing the star failed twice (Gate 0). The agents now do what LLMs are good at: routing, explaining, and checking explanations. Every explanation is checked by the Critic and measured on all 3,000 test reviews. A1 is running; DeBERTa runs on Colab Nov 1. Final demo is a local notebook. |
| 21 | main talk | Phase 2 v3 Build Schedule | Build schedule, Oct 25 to Nov 5. Say: every row has its rule written first and is logged. Today the saved agents were rebuilt and match the frozen results exactly. The heavy runs (bigger probe, explanations on all 3,000 reviews, deletion test) run overnight on the charger. Freeze stage 1 on Nov 1, stage 2 on Nov 5. |
| 22 | main talk | Plan to Submission and the December Final Presentation | Roadmap. Freeze stage 1 Nov 1 (local work), stage 2 Nov 5 (Colab result in or out). Author writes the prose from Nov 2; draft 1 to supervisor Nov 8; submit by Nov 20. December: final presentation with the live demo notebook (Phase 1 and Phase 2). |
